author: The Wall Street Journal
description:
Amateur athletes’ ability to sign endorsement deals that monetize their name, image, and likeness has pumped billions of dollars into college sports. Now it’s coming for high school athletes. 

For some parents and coaches, NIL deals create welcome opportunities for students to offset the growing costs of elite youth sports. Others, especially in the six states that still restrict NIL activity before college, think allowing teenage athletes to cash in on their personal brands takes the increasing professionalization of amateur sports too far.

One company's mission to produce a 100% made-in-America Monopoly game ran into cracked trays, sky-high costs and a dice dilemma after Trump tariffs disrupted Chinese production.⁠
⁠
The Monopoly Americana Edition took nearly 14 months to bring to market and ended up with an $80 price tag, compared with $45 for the China-made version.⁠
